task: Advance the buildbot-sheathing programme: milestone 9, pushing a bowed joint stud onto its line instead of doubling it.

errors.what: The first nail-by-nail push sequence re-pushed the mid point it had already held, so the FE solve reported forces 10^6 times the mid push.
errors.fix: push_sequence skips a point whose dof is already held; caught by comparing max/mid ratios across bows before any result was written.

errors.what: A three-point simultaneous push returned 10^33 N: the uniform node grid and the pushed points coincided to within 1e-16, making a degenerate element.
errors.fix: _nodes drops grid nodes within 1e-6 of a pushed point.

errors.what: The dollars break-even search stopped at 600 s and printed None (no crossing in range).
errors.fix: widened to 3,600 s; the crossing is at 925 s. Re-ran the experiment before writing it up.

A one-line example of reading the path back from the background log would save a step.

deviations.why: The prompt's default is to take a free milestone from the track list; the track-20 draw offered buildbot-sheathing's open milestones, but all 8 listed were done and the README's 'Next steps' asked how far sheathing nails pull a bowed stud straight.
deviations.did: Reframed that open question as a milestone of its own (nails cannot pull a stud straight -- a nail goes in where the stud is -- so the question is a push) and pre-registered H41-H44 before running anything.
deviations.result: Worked: three hypotheses held, one was refuted informatively, and the refutation separated the single-2x cap into two roughly equal halves (bow and sheet pose), which is the result the paper gains most from.

goal: Land one step of an open research programme with a pre-registered, falsifiable result.
notes:
Milestone 9 of the buildbot-sheathing programme. New module src/buildbot_sheathing/straighten.py: an Euler-Bernoulli beam for a Stud-grade 2x4 bending flatwise, solved both in closed form and on a cubic-Hermite FE grid, with E drawn lognormally about the NDS reference values (DF-L 1.4, Hem-Fir 1.2, S-P-F 1.2, SP 1.3 million psi; COV 0.25). Sourced from the AWC NDS Supplement Table 4A as tabulated by Engineers Edge and from SFPA Table 1 (the AWC PDF itself 403s/Cloudflares through the proxy); cross-checked against the tabulated E_min (475,000 against 470,000 published), which is what makes the 0.25 COV more than an assumption.

Results: a mid-height push takes 48 E I b / L^3, median 28 N and p99 126 N at the lower published warp (53/232 N higher, 376 N at the grade limit); a stock G1 can push 81-88 N sideways at that height (ankle roll) and an H1 120-123 N, covering 93%/99% of low-warp studs. Nail-by-nail pushing needs up to 1,258 N because each driven nail shortens the free span: push first, nail after. H43 refuted: straightening lifts the best single-2x pipeline 0.560 -> 0.710 (low warp) and 0.307 -> 0.677 (high), but the same pipeline on perfectly straight studs gives 0.737, so it reaches the ceiling rather than underperforming. That splits the 44-point single-2x deficit into ~18 points of lumber (removable with 28 N) and ~26 points of sheet placement (not).

Verification run here, not read off CI: 66 passed / 4 skipped (the skips need Drake, absent in this image) with /usr/bin/python3.13; paper/check_numbers.py 91 of 91 ok (13 new checks for milestone 9); research/_homepage/build.py ok (1078 projects); check_md_links.py ok; research_live_links.py ok; research-ci.yml 3/3 run steps passed locally; unlanded_work.py exit 0.
